steps.content: Graves follows you into the interrogation room with visible trepidation, like a scolded little animal, anxiously scanning the unfamiliar surroundings.
Before her lies a cramped, dimly lit room filled with surveillance equipment, and at its center stands a single cold chair, seemingly unforgiving.

options: Don't be so hard on yourself.

choices.text: Don't be so hard on yourself.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We're just having a chat. No need to be nervous.
You soften your tone and gesture for her to make herself comfortable in the chair.
As you consider where to begin your questions, Graves breaks the silence first, her face illuminated by the harsh overhead light.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Umm... Are you mad at me?
You shake your head. It's not anger so much as... resignation?
Seeing you remain silent, Graves squirms uncomfortably in her chair, as if sitting on hot coals.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Do I look ridiculous right now? I just wanted to give you a surprise, but I never expected things would turn out like that...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Oh! My hair... and my dress too... This is terribly improper...
Graves attempts to smooth her disheveled hair and straighten her crumpled dress, but there's no hiding the long tear running across the hem.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Oh, no... I can't hide it! I... I need to go back and get changed!
Graves leaps to her feet in agitation, ready to make a dash for the door, but you quickly step forward to block her path.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's just the two of us here. How about we finish our conversation first, then I'll walk you back to change your clothes?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all the trouble you went through to see me, don't you want to talk?
Graves tilts her head, pondering your words. After a few seconds of consideration, she quietly returns to her seat.

You glance at the surveillance camera in the corner and exhale with relief. You, as the MBCC Chief, nearly letting a Sinner escape the interrogation room would surely become the Bureau's latest joke if anyone found out.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Ahem... Now, tell me what happened tonight.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Tonight... tonight I went to see Letta, you know, the girl who sleepwalks with a lantern. She told me many things about you and the Bureau.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: She also told me that exploring the Bureau at night is very exciting, so I just...
Graves, who has been speaking with some excitement, suddenly lowers her voice. Her eyes dart nervously around the room while her fingers fidget aimlessly.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Umm... so I wanted to... explore! Yes, explore!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Letta shared her <color=#fb9259>Bureau exploration tips</color> with me, and I... I just couldn't wait to try them out!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Bureau exploration tips? What on earth is that...
You sift through Graves's fractured explanation, trying to piece together a narrative from the shards.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So you're saying my office and the storage room were both part of your Bureau "exploration"?
Graves nods earnestly, completely unaware that there might be anything wrong with her actions.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Picked up some bad habits from Letta already, huh...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then, can you explain why your "exploration" turned my office into a haunted site? And what exactly were you doing in the storage room? Why try to lure me there?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: These incidents seem completely unrelated. I can't accept "exploration" as an explanation for all of them.
The barrage of questions comes too overwhelming. Graves parrots them back, but can't formulate any coherent answers.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Please don't ask so many questions at once. I can't keep up... Haunted? Where's the ghost?
Graves blinks her big eyes, wearing an expression of complete innocence.
She either doesn't realize how unconvincing her act is, or she simply doesn't want to tell the truth.
You drag a sigh from deep in your chest, feigning sadness as if her evasiveness is a personal betrayal.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I thought... we were close enough to share everything with each other. I never expected you'd feel more loyal to Letta after knowing her for just one day...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: That's not true! We're closer than anyone—nothing compares!
Spurred by your emotional expression, Graves immediately sits up straight, eager to prove her loyalty to you.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Just ask and I won't hide anything from you!

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Really?
Graves nods repeatedly, her gaze as solemn and determined as if she were to make a sacred vow.
The truth is, you genuinely can't parse Graves's logic—what's her motivation for her behavior, why she has been so evasive with her answers.
Is she trying to get your attention? Or does she need to do something to validate her own existence?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Graves, you're now my Sinner, and I have a responsibility to supervise your behavior.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: About tonight... I'm not here to blame you. We can call it a prank, or whatever kind of interaction you wanted to have with me. I just want to understand why you did it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I want to get to know the real you. So don't dodge my questions or be afraid to speak honestly, okay?
You carefully keep any trace of blame out of your voice.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: You promise... you're really not mad at me?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I promise—I'm not angry, and I don't dislike you. I just... want us to really talk.
Your words visibly put Graves at ease. The nervous flutter of her hands stills as she sits up attentively, waiting for your questions.
With the tension diffused, you marshal the night's chaos into order, methodically working through each unanswered question.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Were you the one making those noises in my office? What were you trying to do?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Adjutant Nightingale said you were busy dealing with the aftermath of the castle incident. It's all because of me...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I may not have much experience, but I know that a proper bride should help ease her love's burdens.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: So... I just wanted to help you. I didn't mean to disturb you, really!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I snuck in secretly because I didn't want to distract you...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So those "paranormal activities" happened because you were trying to help me?
Graves nods with an innocent expression, seeming genuinely truthful.

options: Did you move things on my desk?

choices.text: Did you move things on my desk?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: You... noticed it? I thought I did a good job hiding myself...
Graves lowers her head, anxiously interlocking her fingers.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I wanted to bring you water at first, but you were already making coffee, so I thought I'd help tidy up your desk instead.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But I couldn't understand any of your files, so I just moved them around. And, uh... couldn't do it well.
Her tone turns frustrated, clearly dissatisfied with her earlier attempt.

options: What's with that strange massage cushion?

choices.text: What's with that strange massage cushion?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Strange? Is there something wrong with the cushion?
Noticing your peculiar expression, Graves continues to explain.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Sitting too long is bad for your health, so I specifically asked Adjutant Nightingale for a premium cushion... You don't like it?
Graves watches you with an eager, expectant expression, waiting for your answer. But the thought of your skin touching that cushion still prickles your mind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Next time, you can just give me the gift directly.

options: What's with the note written in blood on the window?

choices.text: What's with the note written in blood on the window?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: ...Blood? How could there be blood? Are you hurt?
Graves anxiously examines your hands, only to find no signs of bleeding. You pull the note you took from the window out of your pocket and hand it to her.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: This isn't blood; it's lipstick.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I wanted you to stop working and get some rest, but didn't want to interrupt... so I just stuck the note on your window, hoping you'd notice it.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I saw you holding your head, so I opened the window for you. How was it? Did the cool night breeze make you feel any better?
Graves's explanation leaves you speechless in resignation. You can't help but wonder how on earth she has managed to turn acts of kindness into something straight out of a ghost story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Well, I can see that these are just your unique ways of showing concern. But what were you doing in the storage room? Why did you try to lead me there?
Graves falls silent for a moment, and you notice the tips of her ears slowly turning red. What is it that she finds so difficult to explain?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I... wasn't trying to lead you there... I just haven't fully mastered the Bureau exploration tips, and got caught by you...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Letta taught me how to sneak into your office. In exchange, I had to help find her secret treasure—
In a sheepish manner, she holds up a rubber duck she took from the storage room when leaving.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Letta told me that after a long day of overtime work, soaking in a relaxing hot bath with rubber ducks to play with is the most delightful thing ever.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: So... she promised me that if I found the rubber ducks, she would share some with me...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: So, what do you think? Do you... like it?
Graves's fingers tighten reflexively around the duck—a soft quack escaping as she anxiously watches for your reaction.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So, your original plan was to find rubber ducks in the storage room, then sneak into my room and prepare a bath?
Graves nods sheepishly.
You picture yourself returning to your room after overtime and finding a bathtub filled with water and a flotilla of rubber ducks...
Well, you suppose that would count as a surprise.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I was in the storage room looking for this box of rubber ducks when I heard the door close. I thought someone caught me.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But then no one appeared, so I thought I must have imagined things...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: When I heard your voice, I was terrified—too scared to move or answer... Then I realized you'd mistaken me for an intruder, so I had to come out.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Since I had no choice but to show myself, I was planning to give you a hug to celebrate our reunion, but instead you used your shackles on me.
As she speaks, Graves grows visibly upset. The memory of pain from the shackles still makes her shudder, and her voice takes on a hurt tone.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I'm so sorry, dear. I only meant to do something kind for you. Did I frighten you?
Now that you have learned the whole story, you realize it was all just a misunderstanding.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So who exactly closed the storage room's door?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Hmm... Wasn't it you?
You and Graves exchange bewildered looks, both having assumed the other closed the door. Could this be a genuine paranormal occurrence in the Bureau?
You push aside the creeping unease within you and continue your conversation with Graves.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Anyway... thank you for your kind intentions, Graves.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've made a friend on your first day at the Bureau—that's a good start. Just maybe don't follow Letta's example, wandering around the Bureau in the middle of the night. It can give people quite a fright.
You meant to lighten the mood with a little humor, but your words seem to have brought more unease to Graves instead.
She lowers her head, her long eyelashes casting shadows beneath her eyes, her voice now tinged with melancholy.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Yes... everyone has been so kind—greeting me, showing me around, explaining where to go, when to be there, and who to ask for help...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: This place has everything—comfortable spaces, convenient facilities, new things I've never seen before... It's nothing like the castle...
Though Graves speaks of warm things, the air around her grows ice-cold. The shackles connecting you both begin to tremble faintly.
Sensing Graves's emotional shift, you speak softly to comfort her, guiding the conversation based on her own words.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But is all this actually overwhelming you?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: ...I don't know. I just feel like I have to do something.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: It all feels so unreal. I'm afraid that if I close my eyes, everything will vanish... I'll lose you, lose these new friends, just like what happened in the past...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: If people saw the real me... they would run away screaming, wouldn't they?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: No one wants to be friends with a <color=#fb9259>monster</color>. Not everyone is you, willing to stand by a monster's side.

steps.speaker: Child B
steps.content: Taking things without permission is stealing!

steps.speaker: Child A
steps.content: Ooooh! Not just a stray nobody wants—you're a thief too! No wonder your parents left you!

steps.speaker: Child B
steps.content: Still pretending you're not a monster? If you weren't one, why'd they throw you away?

steps.speaker: Child A
steps.content: Yeah! When that old nun grabbed you, did she even know you were a freaky little monster?

steps.speaker: Guest B
steps.content: What's this filthy monster doing here? Come to ruin the ceremony?

steps.speaker: Guest C
steps.content: She's a damn curse! Get her out of here before she snaps and hurts someone!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Little monster, soft and small, lonely as the dust that falls. No one near to hold her tight, till a nun brought loving light.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Little monster, sweet but feared, eyes would wince when she appeared. Wedding lights shone bright as day, but stones chased her far away.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Little monster, sighs so deep, moonbeams kiss her while she weeps. If her face shone like a star, would love find her where they are?
With eyes closed, Graves gently sways her head, softly murmuring the nursery rhyme she wrote herself.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I really thought this time, I wouldn't be left behind again. I believed Elsie would stay with me forever!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But in the end, she was scared of me too. I was left all alone again...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: After she left, the castle faded into dust, and I became that unwanted little monster again. A monster in a ruined castle... how perfect.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Then, as time went by, new faces came to the castle... No. 15... Dullahan... At last, I had friends who were just like me.
Graves's voice drifts, hazy with recollection.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I made a wish upon the ring, and there you were. You promised you'd never leave, then brought me to the Bureau. I've never been this happy!

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But this place... it's too wonderful. So wonderful that I feel I don't belong here at all...

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I'm so scared. Can a monster like me really keep all this...? Do I really deserve to feel happy?
Graves stretches out her hands. They're empty—hands that have never truly held onto anything. That's why when she finally has something to call her own, it all feels too surreal to be true.
Although you've told her to "embrace herself fully" and to "love herself," years of pain still pull her thoughts toward darker places.
To truly instill belief in this anxious, insecure girl, you must do something, something that's more than just words.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You really are a wonderful person, and you deserve everything you have right now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You don't have to fuss over me or go out of your way to prove anything. I'm the one who failed—I never noticed how insecure you felt.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've had so little to hold onto in life. You're scared that, just like before, this happiness is nothing but another bubble, ready to pop at any time.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: In your world, love always comes with conditions, and being left behind is the norm. But that's wrong.
You deliberately keep your speech slow, as if trying to imprint these words deep into Graves's heart.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You can trust my promises. I will honor every word I've spoken to you. No matter what happens, I won't leave you, and I won't let anyone hurt you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Of course, if you feel the urge to do something to put yourself at ease, to prove everything you have now is real...
You pause for a moment, the corners of your mouth lifting into a faint smile.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then why not just work with me directly?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Work... with you?
She tilts her head in confusion, her voice tinged with uncertainty.
You nod, already having a plan in mind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Even in fairy tales, after the happy ending comes ordinary, everyday life.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Alright, the interrogation is over. As we agreed, I'll walk you back now.
